title: Boundary wall maximum length, R30-R40 all other lots (65% of the lot boundary)
text: C3.4.4 Boundary walls may be built in accordance with Table 3.4c provided: i. boundary walls are located behind the street setback; ii. overshadowing does not exceed the limits of C3.8.1; and iii. they are finished to an equivalent standard to the rest of the development, to the satisfaction of the decision-maker. Table 3.4c Lot boundary setbacks, R30 - R40 all other lots: maximum boundary wall length 65% of the lot boundary; number of boundaries All (Figure 3.4i).

parts.label: access not from a rear right-of-way

exceptions.label: abuts an existing or simultaneously constructed wall of similar or greater dimension (C3.4.5)

replaces.note: two-thirds behind the setback -> 65% of the whole boundary (small tightening); R30-R35 two boundaries -> all (C4P1-094)

verified.note: Value 65% clear. The page does not say whether the 65% is per wall or cumulative per boundary: Figure 3.4i (p35) in this chapter shows one wall per boundary (W1 on A, W2 on B, W3 on C), unlike the Chapter 3 figure which groups W3-W5 on boundary C. The encoded fact is the longest single wall.

notes: from: ch3 C3.4.4#length-r30-r40. Table 3.4c (p34) values unchanged from Chapter 3; the clause text now cites C3.8.1 for overshadowing. All other R30-R40 lots: 65% of the lot boundary, all boundaries. Unclear whether per boundary or cumulative; the fact is per boundary. Boundary walls are single storey at R30-R40, so mainly garages and bin stores for apartments (C4P1-094).
